2.The aforesaid case arose out of a complaint filed by the Food Safety Officer alleging infringement of Section 3(1) (zz)(v) & (vii), Section 26(2)(i) , Section 27(1), Section 38(1) and Section 59(iii) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter referred to as 'the FSS Act, 2006'), read with Regulation 2.12 of the Food Safety and Standards (Food Product Standards and Food Additives)
Regulations, 2011 (hereinafter referred to as "the Regulations, 2011") .

sentences.text: 3.The allegation in the complaint is that the sample of `Fish Fry' purchased for analysis on 19.11.2014 by the 1st respondent from the restaurant "Red Chilies", of which the 1st accused is the food business operator, was reported to be unsafe on analysis by the public analyst as it contained sunset yellow, a synthetic colour, contravening the provisions of the FSS Act, 2006 and the Regulations framed therefrom.
4.The aforesaid proceedings are sought to be quashed invoking the powers of this Court under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal procedure.
5.I have heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner as well as the learned Public Prosecutor.
6.It is submitted by the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner that the petitioner has been arrayed on the sole ground that he was the licencee of the restaurant.
Referring to Annexure-I, it is contended that though on 07/09/2012, license under the FSS Act, 2006 was taken in the name of the petitioner it was valid only till 31/03/2013.

To bring home this point, reliance is placed on Annexure-III communication issued by the Assistant Commissioner of Food Safety, Ernakulam which reveals that the validity of the license issued in the name of the petitioner was from 01/04/2012 to 31/03/2013.

Elaborating further, it is urged by the learned Counsel that the 1st respondent has also not issued any notice to the petitioner calling upon him to exercise his option to prefer an appeal against the report of the food analyst before the designated officer.
The learned counsel drew the attention of this Court to Annexure-V copy of acknowledgment, which reveals that the statutory notice was accepted by the 1st accused for and on behalf of "Red Chillies".

Finally, it is submitted that the sanction was accorded by the Commissioner of Food Safety to prosecute the petitioner by impressing upon the said authority that the statutory notice was served on the petitioner and that he had failed to prefer an appeal under Section 46(4) of the FSS Act, 2006.
7.The learned Public Prosecutor on the other hand refuted the submissions and contended that the petitioner is none other than the brother-in-law of the 1st accused.
Though the petitioner was not in station at the relevant point of time, the licence was initially obtained in his name.
No prejudice has been caused to the petitioner and the grounds raised by the petitioner is not sufficient to quash the proceedings, is the submission.
8.I have considered the rival submissions and have gone through the materials on record.

sentences.text: 3 9.Annexure-I is the complaint filed by the Food Safety Officer, Thripunithura Circle which speaks about the inspection which was conducted on 19.11.2014 in the "Red Chillies" restraurant.
The specific contention of the petitioner is that though the license was initially taken in his name, the same was valid only till 31.3.2013.
Annexure-III communication issued by the Assistant Commissioner of Food Safety, Ernakulam emphatically supports the above assertion of the petitioner.
Therefore it cannot be said that as on the date of inspection, the petitioner was the licensee of the restaurant.
10.It is in section 46 (4) of the FSS Act , that the functions of the Food Analyst is enumerated .
The analyst , within a period of 14 days from the date of receipt of the same for analysis is bound to send the report of analysis to the designated officer.

There is a statutory right of appeal against the report of the Food Analyst before the Designated officer, who is empowered, to refer the matter to the referral food laboratory as notified by the Food Authority for opinion.

In the case on hand, it is stated in the complaint that the notice calling upon the accused Nos. 1 and 2 to exercise their right under section 46 (4) of the Food Safety Act was issued to the petitioner as well.

However,
Annexure-V acknowledgment would reveal that the said notice was accepted by the 1st accused for and on behalf of "Red Chillies".

The assertion of the learned Counsel that the sanction was obtained from the appropriate authority for prosecuting the petitioner by making it appear that the notice was served on the petitioner and that he had not cared to prefer the appeal as mandated under law cannot be ignored as such.
In other words the sanction to prosecute the petitioner was secured by suppressing the above fact.
I have no doubt in my mind that the prosecution of the petitioner, in the facts and circumstances is not justified.

11.In that view of the matter, I am of the considered view that this is an eminently fit case for invocation of the inherent power under Section 482 of the Code in the interest of justice, as the prosecution of the petitioner is only an abuse of process.
In the result, this petition is allowed.

Annexure-1 complaint and all further proceedings against the petitioner, who is the 2nd accused, in C.C. No. 3605 of 2015 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate, Thripunithura are quashed.
